title: Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery: Installment Relief After a Recent Fall in Disability Compensation
content:
A recent fall in a debtor's **Disability Compensation** lowers the monthly installment of a direct-payment repayment plan on a debt in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery**.

**Rule.** When the monthly compensation payments of the last six calendar months counted back from today add up to more than that many months at the award's current veteran-alone monthly rate and the award is rated 60 percent or more, the higher relief rate of 95 percent applies. When they add up to more and the award is rated below 60 percent, the lower relief rate of 90 percent applies. Otherwise no relief rate applies under this rule.

**Reading the records.**

- *Payments of the last six months*: the gross amounts of the monthly Disability Compensation payments whose payment date falls in the period, and their number. A payment falls in the period when fewer than six whole calendar months have passed from its payment date to today.
- *Current rate*: the veteran-alone monthly rate of the debtor's running award, taken as zero where no award is running; the rating is that award's combined rating.
- *Comparison*: the total of those payments is compared with their number multiplied by the current rate; only a total strictly above that product counts.

The relief rate is a percentage by which the quotient of the balance to be spread and the months is multiplied before the installment is rounded up to the cent.

## Hypothetical cases

| Payments in the period | Current rate | Rating | Relief rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 payments totalling 10,500.00 USD | 1,663.06 USD (6 months: 9,978.36 USD) | 70 percent | 95 percent |
| Same | 1,102.04 USD | 50 percent | 90 percent |
| 6 payments totalling 9,978.36 USD | 1,663.06 USD | 70 percent | None — equal, not more |
